en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Ants.
9. The Question on the Boar’s Limbs “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two limbs of a boar should be taken,’ which are those two limbs that should be taken?
“Just as, Great King, when the summer season has arrived and the ground is parched and heated, a boar goes toward the water;”

In the same way, Great King, when the mind of a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, has been agitated, faltered, distracted, and heated by hatred, he should resort to the cool, sweet, and sublime meditation on loving-kindness (*mettā*).
This, Great King, is the first quality of the boar that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the boar, having approached a muddy pool and dug into the earth with its snout, makes a trough and lies down within that hollow.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin practicing yoga, having laid down the body in the mind, should lie down with his attention directed toward another object.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the boar that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja:
Having seen the intrinsic nature of the body and having investigated it,
The ninth inquiry, the Question on the Boar’s Limb.
